title: Antidepressant mechanism of secoisolariciresinol in corticosterone-induced mice: PTGS2 as a key target of the cAMP-PKA-CREB-BDNF pathway.
authors: Tuo, Yan-Jun; Meng, Zi; A, Ru-Han; Zhai, Shu-Ting; Wang, Mu-Lan; Zha, Chen-Liang; Zou, En-Guo; He, Bei-Lan; Feng, Ye-Meng; Zeng, Xiao-Long; Li, Jun; Gong, Qin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然单体SECO的抗抑郁机制，涉及分子对接但核心为信号通路与动物实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Secoisolariciresinol (SECO), a natural monomer from Syringa oblata Lindl, remains unclear in antidepressant effects. This study aimed to investigate the antidepressant mechanism of SECO and clarify its core target and signaling pathway. METHODS: Network pharmacology, molecular docking and corticosterone (CORT)-induced depressive mice model were applied. Behavioral tests, histological staining, ELISA and Western blot were performed for evaluation. RESULTS: Behavioral tests confirmed that SECO significantly improved depressive-like behaviors, increased sucrose preference and exploratory ability, and reduced immobility time. SECO ameliorated hippocampal CA1 neuronal morphological damage and neuronal loss. Treatment with SECO significantly decreased serum corticosterone (CORT) concentrations and hippocampal prostaglandin E(2) (PGE(2)) levels. Concurrently, it elevated serum levels of key neurotransmitters, namely serotonin (5-HT), norepinephrine (NE), and dopamine (DA), and increased cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) content in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, SECO downregulated the expression of prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2) and activated the cAMP-PKA-CREB-BDNF signaling cascade. CONCLUSION: SECO alleviates neuroinflammation via PTGS2 inhibition and enhances neuronal plasticity by activating the cAMP/PKA-CREB-BDNF signaling pathway. These two synergistic effects contribute to the neuroprotective action of SECO, thereby ameliorating CORT-induced depressive-like behaviors in mice.
abstract_zh: 目的：紫丁香苷元（SECO）是从紫丁香（Syringa oblata Lindl）中提取的天然单体，其抗抑郁作用尚不明确。本研究旨在探讨SECO的抗抑郁机制，并明确其核心靶点和信号通路。方法：采用网络药理学、分子对接和皮质酮（CORT）诱导的抑郁小鼠模型。通过行为学测试、组织学染色、ELISA和Western blot进行评估。结果：行为学测试证实，SECO显著改善抑郁样行为，增加蔗糖偏好和探索能力，并减少不动时间。SECO改善海马CA1区神经元形态损伤和神经元丢失。SECO治疗显著降低血清皮质酮（CORT）浓度和海马前列腺素E(2)（PGE(2)）水平。同时，它提高了血清中关键神经递质，即血清素（5-HT）、去甲肾上腺素（NE）和多巴胺（DA）的水平，并增加了海马中环磷酸腺苷（cAMP）含量。机制上，SECO下调前列腺素内过氧化物合酶2（PTGS2）的表达，并激活cAMP-PKA-CREB-BDNF信号级联。结论：SECO通过抑制PTGS2减轻神经炎症，并通过激活cAMP/PKA-CREB-BDNF信号通路增强神经元可塑性。这两种协同效应有助于SECO的神经保护作用，从而改善CORT诱导的小鼠抑郁样行为。
